MESSAGE:
Hi. I'm off to Lisbon next week for a three-day work trip, my first time in Portugal, and I want to travel carry-on only this time, after the airline lost my case in the spring.

Could you suggest three things to do in Lisbon on a free evening? And how do I say "thank you" in Portuguese? Is it different depending on who's saying it? And is tipping expected in restaurants there, or is that more of an American thing?

My wheeled bag measures 56 × 36 × 23 cm including the wheels and handle, and packed it weighs 9 kg. Will it meet the carry-on limit?

Also, recommend a packing approach: rolling or folding for work shirts? I need a short out-of-office message that's professional but not stiff, since most of my contacts are clients rather than colleagues. And what's a good colour for a luggage tag so it's easy to spot? I'm flying back on the Friday evening, straight after a full day of meetings, so anything that makes the return journey less stressful is welcome.

Thanks a lot.

REQUESTS:
1. Suggest three things to do in Lisbon in the evening
2. Explain how to say 'thank you' in Portuguese and whether it varies by speaker
3. Say whether tipping is expected in Lisbon restaurants
4. Determine whether a 56 x 36 x 23 cm, 9 kg bag meets the carry-on limit  KEY: Missing datum: the airline (and fare type) is not stated, and carry-on size/weight limits vary by airline and fare, so this cannot be confirmed. Should ask which airline/fare and illustrate: under a common 55 x 40 x 20 cm limit the bag fails (56 > 55 length, 23 > 20 depth); under a 56 x 45 x 25 cm limit it fits; weight limits range roughly 7-10 kg, so 9 kg may exceed a 7 or 8 kg limit.
5. Recommend rolling vs folding shirts
6. Write a short out-of-office message
7. Suggest a luggage tag colour

ANSWER:
## Three things for a free evening

1. **Watch the sunset from a miradouro (viewpoint).** Miradouro da Senhora do Monte and Santa Luzia have some of the best views over the city's rooftops and the river. Then walk down into Alfama.
2. **Dinner with fado in Alfama.** Fado is Portugal's traditional music, sad and very atmospheric. Many small restaurants have live sets in the evening. Book ahead if you can, and expect to stay quiet while the singer performs.
3. **Food and a drink in Bairro Alto or at Time Out Market.** Time Out Market is easy if you're on your own and short on time, since you can try lots of local dishes in one place. Afterwards, Bairro Alto's narrow streets fill up with people drinking outside the bars. Have a pastel de nata (custard tart) at some point.

## "Thank you" in Portuguese

It depends on **who's speaking**, not who you're thanking:
- **Obrigado** (oh-bree-GAH-doo) if you're a man
- **Obrigada** (oh-bree-GAH-dah) if you're a woman

"Muito obrigado/a" means "thank you very much."

## Tipping

It isn't expected the way it is in the US, and service usually isn't added to the bill. People in Portugal often round up, or leave about **5–10% for good service** in a sit-down restaurant. In cafés, leaving small change is fine. Nobody will mind if you don't tip.

## Will your bag fit? That depends on the airline

Your bag is **56 × 36 × 23 cm and 9 kg**. Some common limits for comparison (check your booking, since airlines change these):

| Airline (standard cabin bag) | Limit | Your bag |
|---|---|---|
| British Airways | 56 × 45 × 25 cm, 23 kg | Fits |
| easyJet (large cabin bag, paid add-on) | 56 × 45 × 25 cm, 15 kg | Fits, if you've paid for it |
| TAP Air Portugal | 55 × 40 × 20 cm, 8 kg | **Too big and too heavy** |
| Ryanair (Priority) | 55 × 40 × 20 cm, 10 kg | **Too big** (1 cm too long, 3 cm too deep) |

Tell me which airline you're flying with and I'll check it properly. On stricter airlines, the 23 cm depth is the measurement most likely to cause a problem.

## Packing work shirts

**Fold them rather than rolling.** Rolling is fine for T-shirts and casual clothes, but it leaves creases in crisp shirts. Fold each one around a sheet of tissue paper or inside a packing folder, and lay them flat on top. When you arrive, hang them in the bathroom while you shower and the steam will drop most creases out.

## Out-of-office message

> Thank you for your email. I'm travelling for work from [date] to [date] with limited access to email, so my replies may be slower than usual. I'll get back to you as soon as I can after I return on [date]. If your query is urgent, please contact [name] at [email/phone].
>
> Best wishes,
> [Your name]

## Luggage tag colour

**Bright fluorescent orange or lime green.** Very few bags are those colours, so it stands out on a carousel.

Even with carry-on only, a tag still matters. On busy flights, wheeled cabin bags are often checked at the gate when the overhead bins fill up. Keep your laptop, passport, chargers and any medication in a small personal bag that stays with you.

## Making the Friday return easier

- **Pack the night before** and check out in the morning. Leave your bag with the hotel's luggage storage and collect it after your meetings.
- **The metro's red line goes straight to the airport**, about 20–25 minutes from the centre. It's often quicker than a taxi on a Friday evening.
- **Allow extra time at the airport.** Lisbon gets busy on Friday evenings. If you're travelling on a UK or other non-EU passport, the EU's new Entry/Exit System can make passport queues longer, so leave plenty of time.
- **Check in online and keep your boarding pass on your phone.** Keep your liquids bag near the top of your case so it's quick to pull out at security.

Have a good trip.
